title: Initiating a project: the seven activities and the PID
blurb: Name the seven activities of initiating a project, why they run in that order and how they come together in the PID.
question: In which activity of initiating a project is the outline business case updated with the time and cost from the project plan?

teach.body: Formally: initiating a project has seven activities, from agreeing the tailoring requirements to requesting project authorization. In plain English: decide how the method will be used here, agree the rules for managing the project, set up controls, plan the whole project, firm up the business case, check it all fits together as the PID, then ask the board to commit.

teach.caption: Older names: set up project controls, create the project plan, refine the business case.

teach.body: The management approaches come from the business strategies, standards or practices the project must follow, plus the users' quality and sustainability expectations in the project product description. Lessons from similar projects are sought too. Once the approaches exist, project controls and the project plan can be set up. The full business case then uses the plan's time and cost and the aggregated risks from the project log.

head: Approach
Practice home
teach.caption: All nine are agreed in 'agree the management approaches'. The change management approach is about organizational transition, not change control.

items: Agree the tailoring requirements: adapt PRINCE2 or the business's own method to internal and external factors; how it is applied must be documented and agreed.
Establish project controls: agree how much control the board needs after initiation and how it will work, and the PM's control over team managers' work.
Assemble the PID: cross-check its parts for compatibility; the version used for authorization is baselined and put under change control.
Request project authorization: ask the board for authority to deliver, with or without a formal meeting.

values: Project plan time and cost; project log risks

teach.h: Worked scenario: a student records system
teach.body: At Stonebridge University, project manager Aisha Patel starts initiation by agreeing with the board to merge two reports and send highlight reports fortnightly. She agrees the nine approaches, using lessons from the estates team's last contract for the commercial approach. With controls set, she prepares the project plan, then updates the business case with its costs and the aggregated risks. She cross-checks everything, assembles the PID and requests authorization.

teach.text: Classic traps: the full business case comes AFTER the project plan, because it needs the plan's time and cost. The executive (not the business layer) is accountable for it. The risk management approach describes the procedure; specific risks go in the risk register. The change management approach is organizational transition; change control sits in the issue management approach.

items: Seven activities: tailoring; management approaches; project controls; project plan; full business case; assemble the PID; request project authorization.
Approaches first, then controls and plan, then the full business case.
Nine approaches: benefits, change, commercial, communication, digital and data, issue, quality, risk, sustainability.
The PID is cross-checked, and the authorized version is baselined under change control.

summary: You can now list the seven activities of initiating a project in order, explain why the approaches come before controls and the plan and why the full business case follows the plan, and describe how the PID is assembled and baselined.

A.q: Which is the first activity of initiating a project?
A.why: Initiating a project begins with agree the tailoring requirements (15.4.1), deciding how PRINCE2 or the business's method will be applied.

whyNot.1: The project plan is prepared after the approaches and controls are agreed.
whyNot.2: Agreeing the management approaches is the second activity.
whyNot.3: Project controls are established once the approaches are defined.

A.q: In which activity is the outline business case updated with the time and cost from the project plan?
A.why: Prepare the full business case updates the outline business case with the time and cost from the project plan and aggregated risks from the project log (15.4.5).

whyNot.0: Preparing the project plan produces the time and cost estimates, but the business case is updated in the next activity.
whyNot.2: Assembling the PID cross-checks and gathers products; it does not rewrite the business case.
whyNot.3: Establishing project controls sets the board's and PM's levels of control.

A.q: Which activity agrees the level of control the board needs after initiation and the mechanism for it?
A.why: Establish project controls agrees the board's level of control after initiation and its mechanism, plus the PM's control over team managers' work (15.4.3).

whyNot.0: Tailoring decides how the method is adapted to the project; it is not where the board's control level is set.
whyNot.1: The management approaches set procedures for areas such as risk and quality, not the board's level of control.
whyNot.3: Requesting authorization asks the board to commit; controls are already in place by then.

B.q:
Which two statements about the 'prepare the full business case' activity are correct?
1. The executive is accountable.
2. The business layer is accountable.
3. The project manager is responsible.
4. Project assurance is responsible.
B.why: The executive is accountable (1) and the project manager responsible (3) for preparing the full business case (15.6, tab 15.2).

whyNot.0: Statement 2 is false: the business layer has no involvement in this activity.
whyNot.2: Both are false: the business layer is not involved and project assurance is consulted.
whyNot.3: Statement 4 is false: project assurance is consulted, not responsible.

B.q: Which is NOT one of the nine management approaches agreed in initiating a project?
B.why: PRINCE2 7 has nine approaches: benefits, change, commercial, communication, digital and data, issue, quality, risk and sustainability. A configuration management approach is not one of them.

whyNot.0: The digital and data management approach is one of the nine, linked to the progress practice.
whyNot.1: The sustainability management approach is one of the nine, linked to the business case practice.
whyNot.2: The commercial management approach is one of the nine, linked to the organizing practice.

B.q: What happens when the project initiation documentation is assembled?
options: It is sent to the business layer for approval
Its parts are approved one by one by the PM
Its parts are cross-checked for compatibility
It replaces the business case with the plan
B.why: Assembling the PID includes cross-checking its elements for compatibility; the version used for authorization is then baselined (15.4.6).

whyNot.0: The PID is approved by the project board in authorize the project, not by the business layer.
whyNot.1: The PM assembles the PID, but approval of it is a board decision.
whyNot.3: The business case and project plan are separate parts of the PID; neither replaces the other.

C.q: From which sources are the management approaches derived in 'agree the management approaches'?
options: The project plan's schedule and the stage plans for each stage
Business strategies and standards, and expectations in the PPD
The risk register's entries and the issue register's entries
The team managers' work package descriptions and team plans
C.why: The approaches are derived from the business strategies, standards or practices the project must comply with and the users' quality and sustainability expectations in the PPD (15.4.2).

whyNot.0: The project plan is prepared after the approaches, so it cannot be their source.
whyNot.2: Registers record specific risks and issues; the approaches define how such items will be managed.
whyNot.3: Work packages and team plans come in delivery stages, long after the approaches are agreed.

C.q: A project manager prepares the full business case before any project plan exists. Why is this a problem?
options: The full business case must be approved by the business layer first
The full business case is prepared in starting up a project instead
The full business case must wait until the PID is baselined
The full business case needs time and cost from the project plan
C.why: The full business case is updated with the estimated time and cost determined by the project plan, so the plan has to come first (15.4.5).

whyNot.0: The executive is accountable for the full business case; the business layer has no involvement in preparing it.
whyNot.1: Starting up a project prepares the outline business case; the full version belongs to initiation.
whyNot.2: The full business case is part of the PID, so it cannot wait for the PID to be baselined.

C.q: Which practice is applied in initiating a project when the product breakdown structure, work breakdown structure and product flow diagram are developed?
C.why: Tab 15.3 lists developing the PBS, WBS and product flow diagram under the plans practice.

whyNot.1: Quality is about the quality management approach and quality specifications, not breakdown structures.
whyNot.2: Progress covers controls and reporting, not product breakdown.
whyNot.3: Organizing is applied in initiation by updating the project management team structure.

reteach.title: Rules, then plan, then case
reteach.question: Why can't the full business case be the first thing written in initiation?

blocks.body: First decide how the method fits this project (tailoring). Then write the rulebook for managing it (the approaches). With the rules known, set up controls and plan the whole project. The plan gives time and cost, so now the business case can be made full. Finally, check everything fits as the PID and ask the board to commit.

blocks.text: The PID is not a new document written from scratch: it is the cross-checked collection of products created or updated during initiation.

explain.body: The PM may need to tailor PRINCE2, or the business's standard method, to internal and external factors that affect delivery. However it is applied or tailored, it must be documented and agreed.

test.q: What must happen to the way PRINCE2 is applied or tailored on the project?
options: It must be documented and agreed
It must be approved by team managers
It must copy the previous project
It must be approved by the business layer
test.why: How PRINCE2 or the business's method is applied or tailored must be documented and agreed (15.4.1).

whyNot.1: Team managers do not approve the project's tailoring.
whyNot.2: Tailoring reflects this project's own internal and external factors, not a copy of another project.
whyNot.3: Tailoring decisions are recorded in the PID and approved by the project board when it authorizes the project.

explain.body: Nine approaches: benefits, change, commercial, communication, digital and data, issue, quality, risk and sustainability. They come from business strategies, standards and practices and the expectations in the PPD, informed by lessons from similar projects.

test.q: Which management approach sets out how issues are captured and how changes to baselines are controlled?
test.why: The issue management approach covers how issues are captured and handled, including change control of baselines.

whyNot.0: The change management approach covers organizational transition, not change control.
whyNot.2: The risk management approach covers how risks are managed.
whyNot.3: The quality management approach covers quality techniques, standards and responsibilities.

explain.h: Controls, plan and full business case
explain.body: Establish project controls for the board and the PM, prepare the project plan, then prepare the full business case from the plan's time and cost and the aggregated risks in the updated project log. The executive is accountable and the PM responsible.

test.q: What is taken from the updated project log when the full business case is prepared?
test.why: The full business case reflects the aggregated risks from the updated project log, with time and cost from the project plan (15.4.5).

whyNot.0: Lessons are sought for each activity, but the business case takes the aggregated risks.
whyNot.1: Quality review results are recorded in the quality register and do not feed the business case here.
whyNot.3: Product status sits in the product register and is not what the business case aggregates.

explain.h: Assemble the PID and request authorization
explain.body: Cross-check the parts of the PID for compatibility; the version used to gain authorization is baselined and placed under change control. Then the PM contacts the board to request authority to deliver the project, which ends the initiation stage.

test.q: How does the project manager end the initiating a project process?
options: By issuing the project authorization notice
By authorizing the first work package
By requesting project initiation from the board
By requesting project authorization from the board
test.why: Initiation ends with request project authorization: the PM asks the board for authority to deliver the project (15.4.7).

whyNot.0: The project authorization notice is issued by the board in authorize the project.
whyNot.1: Work packages are authorized in controlling a stage, after the project is authorized.
whyNot.2: Requesting project initiation ends starting up a project, not initiating a project.
